inputs.text: Bloomberg’s own framing gives the game away: as energy prices rise, flights are canceled, and death and destruction dominate the screens, people worldwide are asking when the Iran war will stop. Yet Israel is presented as the exception, with strong public backing to see it through. That contrast is doing useful work: it makes an ongoing war sound like public resolve rather than a choice being sustained by powerful interests. The account doesn’t even finish the thought after “until,” but the omission only sharpens the question of who benefits from keeping this going.

output.main_topic: Critical framing of public attitudes toward the continuation of the Iran war
subtopics: Questions about who benefits from continuing the war
